page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-128 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 172,613.68 and a PassMark CPU score of 89,602.52. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient for small cached blocks, reaching 8,132.17 GB/sec, while large-block uncached reads and writes achieve strong rates of 263.09 GB/sec and 131.24 GB/sec respectively. The server also demonstrates strong capabilities in cryptography, database operations, and static web serving. However, due to the limited memory allocation per core, large-scale LLM text generation is a notable bottleneck, with the 70B model text generation falling into the bottom 25% at 2.67 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-highcpu-128 provides high compute density relative to its memory footprint, making it a viable option for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive RAM arrays. It is highly suited for parallel processing workloads, software compilation, ray tracing, and high-throughput web serving. Conversely, it is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-128 is a compute-optimized x86_64 server configured with 128 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. With a 1:1 ratio of gigabytes to vCPUs, this instance is designed for highly parallel, CPU-bound tasks. It lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core CPU performance, strong memory bandwidth, and excellent ray tracing capabilities. However, the low memory-to-core ratio limits its effectiveness for memory-heavy applications, as evidenced by weak performance in large LLM text generation. This server is highly efficient for parallel processing, software compilation, and static web serving, but is not recommended for memory-intensive databases.
